weeks.learncpp: Chapters 0–2: setup, compiling, program structure, variables, I/O, functions, parameters, scope, namespaces, headers, multi-file programs.
weeks.dsa: None yet. Protect this week for C++ fundamentals.
weeks.patterns: None.
weeks.implementation: Calculator, temperature converter, prime checker, Fibonacci, and a small multi-file CLI program.
weeks.checkpoint: Compile from the terminal; create functions without copying syntax; explain declaration vs definition; use headers correctly.

weeks.learncpp: Chapters 3–8: debugging, fundamental types, const/constexpr, strings/string_view, operators, scope/lifetime/linkage, control flow and loops.
weeks.dsa: Optional preview: complexity vocabulary only.
weeks.patterns: None.
weeks.implementation: Number guessing game, string utilities, frequency counter, and 10 short loop/function exercises.
weeks.checkpoint: Use debugger/breakpoints; confidently write loops, conditions, strings, const variables and basic functions.

weeks.learncpp: Chapters 9–11: testing/assertions, conversions, type deduction/auto, overloads, default arguments, function templates.
weeks.dsa: Complexity / Big-O module. Learn time vs space, common growth rates, amortized analysis, and how to analyze loops.
weeks.patterns: Basic array scanning and hashing intuition.
weeks.implementation: Write functions using overloads/templates; manually analyze 10 snippets for Big-O.
weeks.checkpoint: For every solved problem, state brute force, optimized approach, time complexity and space complexity.

weeks.learncpp: Chapter 12 in depth: lvalues/rvalues, references, const references, pointers, nullptr, pointer constness, pass-by-reference/address, return by reference/address, std::optional.
weeks.dsa: Arrays module.
weeks.patterns: Array traversal, in-place modification, greedy basics.
weeks.implementation: Simplified dynamic array; pointer/reference drills; trace addresses and object lifetimes on paper.

problems.title: Remove Duplicates from Sorted Array II
Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock
Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock II

weeks.checkpoint: Explain pointer vs reference, pass-by-value vs const reference, nullptr, and why dangling references/pointers are dangerous.

weeks.learncpp: Chapters 13–14: enums/structs, classes, encapsulation, constructors, initializer lists, copy constructor, explicit.
weeks.dsa: Arrays and Strings; begin searching/sorting concepts if included in your current course.
weeks.patterns: Two Pointers, prefix/frequency ideas.
weeks.implementation: Create small class types; write custom comparison helpers; implement two-pointer templates.
weeks.checkpoint: Given a sorted-array problem, identify when two pointers are better than nested loops.

weeks.learncpp: Chapters 15–16: destructors/class details and std::vector. Prioritize vector construction, indexing, iteration, resizing/capacity, passing/returning vectors.
weeks.dsa: Dynamic arrays / arrays and string problems.
weeks.patterns: Sliding Window; fixed vs variable windows.
weeks.implementation: Vector-based utility library; implement fixed-size and variable-size sliding-window templates.

problems.title: Find the Index of the First Occurrence in a String
Two Sum II - Input Array Is Sorted

weeks.checkpoint: Recognize substring/subarray constraints that can be maintained incrementally with a window.

weeks.learncpp: Chapter 17: std::array, C-style arrays, array decay, pointer arithmetic, multidimensional arrays. Do not over-invest in C strings.
weeks.dsa: Linked Lists module.
weeks.patterns: Fast & Slow Pointers; In-place Reversal of a Linked List.
weeks.implementation: SinglyLinkedList and DoublyLinkedList: insert, delete, search, reverse.

problems.title: Remove Nth Node From End of List
Remove Duplicates from Sorted List II

weeks.checkpoint: Reverse a linked list from memory and explain every pointer mutation.

weeks.learncpp: Chapter 18 plus practical STL algorithms: iterators, sort, find, lower_bound/upper_bound; learn stack, queue and deque interfaces.
weeks.dsa: Stack and Queue modules.
weeks.patterns: Stack, Monotonic Stack, expression evaluation, linked-list reversal reinforcement.
weeks.implementation: Implement Stack and Queue yourself, then solve equivalent tasks with std::stack/std::queue.
weeks.checkpoint: Know when a monotonic stack turns an O(n²) nearest-greater/smaller search into O(n).

weeks.goal: Hash tables and associative STL containers
weeks.learncpp: Practical STL focus: unordered_map, map, unordered_set, set, pair, tuple, custom hash/comparator basics. Use cppreference as needed.
weeks.dsa: Hash Table / Hashing module.
weeks.patterns: Hashing, frequency maps, set membership.
weeks.implementation: Simplified hash table using separate chaining; experiment with collisions and load factor.
weeks.checkpoint: Explain average O(1) vs worst-case behavior and when ordered map/set is worth O(log n).

weeks.learncpp: Chapters 19–20: new/delete, dynamic arrays, stack vs heap, recursion, lambdas. Understand manual allocation mainly to understand ownership; prefer RAII in real code.
weeks.dsa: Recursion plus Matrix/Interval-related lessons available in the DSA/pattern courses.
weeks.patterns: Recursion, Matrix Traversal, Merge Intervals.
weeks.implementation: Recursive tree-like exercises; matrix traversal helpers; interval merge from scratch.
weeks.checkpoint: Trace a recursive call stack and explain stack vs heap without hand-waving.

weeks.learncpp: Maintenance only: 20–30 min/day reviewing references, pointers, classes and vectors through DSA code.
weeks.dsa: Trees / Binary Trees module.
weeks.patterns: Tree DFS: preorder, inorder, postorder; recursive tree decomposition.
weeks.implementation: BinaryTree with traversals, height, node count and recursive search.

problems.title: Construct Binary Tree from Preorder and Inorder Traversal
Construct Binary Tree from Inorder and Postorder Traversal
Populating Next Right Pointers in Each Node II
Flatten Binary Tree to Linked List

weeks.checkpoint: Write preorder/inorder/postorder recursively without notes; explain O(n) traversal cost.

weeks.learncpp: Maintenance: classes, ownership and iterators as they appear in tree code.
weeks.dsa: Binary Search Tree module.
weeks.patterns: BST invariants, Tree DFS, LCA, construction from traversals.
weeks.implementation: BST insert, search, delete, min/max, predecessor/successor.

problems.title: Lowest Common Ancestor of a Binary Tree
Kth Smallest Element in a BST

weeks.checkpoint: Explain why inorder traversal of a BST is sorted and derive BST validation correctly.

weeks.learncpp: STL priority_queue and comparator practice.
weeks.dsa: Heap / Priority Queue module.
weeks.patterns: Tree BFS, Top K Elements, Two Heaps.
weeks.implementation: Binary heap with push/pop/heapify; compare against std::priority_queue.

problems.title: Average of Levels in Binary Tree
Binary Tree Zigzag Level Order Traversal
Kth Largest Element in an Array
Find K Pairs with Smallest Sums

weeks.checkpoint: Derive heap operation complexities and explain when a heap beats full sorting.

weeks.learncpp: Use vector<vector<int>>, unordered_map and queue fluently in graph code.
weeks.dsa: Graphs module.
weeks.patterns: Graph DFS/BFS, Island/Matrix Traversal, Topological Sort.
weeks.implementation: Adjacency list + adjacency matrix; BFS, DFS and topological sort.
weeks.checkpoint: Detect cycles and decide BFS vs DFS based on the problem rather than habit.

weeks.learncpp: No major new chapter; reinforce object ownership and container selection.
weeks.dsa: Trie and Disjoint Set/Union-Find material where available; continue graphs.
weeks.patterns: Union Find, Trie, Graph BFS, K-way Merge / divide-and-conquer exposure.
weeks.implementation: Trie and UnionFind (path compression + union by rank/size).

problems.title: Design Add and Search Words Data Structure
Convert Sorted Array to Binary Search Tree

weeks.checkpoint: Implement Union-Find from memory and explain near-constant amortized behavior at interview level.

weeks.goal: Advanced graph algorithms + divide & conquer + greedy/Kadane
weeks.learncpp: C++ maintenance only.
weeks.dsa: Sorting/searching/graph algorithm lessons. Learn Dijkstra, shortest-path concepts, MST, Kruskal and Prim at interview depth.
weeks.patterns: Divide & Conquer, Kadane, Greedy, Merge Intervals reinforcement.
weeks.implementation: Dijkstra, Kruskal or Prim, merge sort, and Kadane from scratch.

problems.title: Minimum Number of Arrows to Burst Balloons

weeks.checkpoint: Know the preconditions and failure cases of BFS shortest path vs Dijkstra vs Bellman-Ford conceptually.

weeks.learncpp: std::lower_bound, std::upper_bound, custom comparators and iterator arithmetic.
weeks.dsa: Binary Search / searching module.
weeks.patterns: Modified Binary Search; binary search on answer; rotated arrays.
weeks.implementation: Write reusable binary-search templates for exact, lower-bound, upper-bound and answer-space search.

problems.title: Find First and Last Position of Element in Sorted Array
Find Minimum in Rotated Sorted Array

weeks.checkpoint: Derive loop invariants and boundaries instead of memorizing one binary-search template.

weeks.learncpp: References, vector mutation, recursion and lambdas as used in backtracking.
weeks.dsa: Backtracking / Subsets material.
weeks.patterns: Subsets, combinations, permutations, choose-explore-unchoose.
weeks.implementation: Generic backtracking skeleton; subsets, permutations and combinations from scratch.

problems.title: Letter Combinations of a Phone Number
Substring with Concatenation of All Words

weeks.checkpoint: Explain state, choices, constraints, base case and undo step for a new backtracking problem.

weeks.learncpp: No major new language material; write clean vectors/memo tables in C++.
weeks.dsa: DP fundamentals / 1D DP material available in your courses.
weeks.patterns: Memoization, tabulation, Fibonacci-style DP, 0/1-style state thinking.
weeks.implementation: Implement memoized and bottom-up versions of 4 classic DP problems.
weeks.checkpoint: For a DP problem, explicitly identify state, transition, base cases and computation order.

weeks.learncpp: C++ maintenance; 2D vector and memory-layout awareness.
weeks.dsa: 2D DP, subsequence/string DP and knapsack-family concepts.
weeks.patterns: Grid DP, sequence DP, string DP.
weeks.implementation: LCS or edit-distance table, grid DP, LIS variants.

problems.title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock III

weeks.checkpoint: Translate a recursive recurrence into memoization and then tabulation.

weeks.goal: Modern C++ ownership + advanced interview patterns
weeks.learncpp: Chapter 21 selectively; Chapter 22 thoroughly: shallow/deep copy, rvalue references, move constructors/assignment, std::move, unique_ptr, shared_ptr, weak_ptr.
weeks.dsa: Finish every remaining core pattern module in your current Grokking course that has not been covered.
weeks.patterns: Bit manipulation, advanced DP, Two Heaps/Top K/K-way Merge review, weak-pattern repair.
weeks.implementation: Small RAII ownership exercise using unique_ptr; implement move-aware class if time allows.

problems.title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock IV

weeks.checkpoint: Explain RAII, ownership, move semantics and why unique_ptr should usually be preferred over shared_ptr.

weeks.learncpp: Selected Chapters 23–28: composition/relationships, inheritance, virtual functions, templates/classes, exceptions, I/O. Read for conceptual fluency; do not let low-interview-value details crowd out problem review.
weeks.dsa: Complete unfinished DSA lessons and pattern lessons; create one-page pattern cue sheet.
weeks.patterns: Full pattern review; no major new pattern.
weeks.implementation: Re-implement two weak data structures from memory and do at least two timed mock sessions.
weeks.checkpoint: 150/150 target complete; explain solutions aloud; identify weak areas for Month 6.

completion: LearnCpp Chapters **0–22** completed at interview-relevant depth.
LearnCpp Chapters **23–28** covered selectively for conceptual fluency.
Design Gurus **Grokking Data Structures & Algorithms for Coding Interviews** core curriculum completed.
All major pattern families in **Grokking the Coding Interview** completed.
**LeetCode Top Interview 150: 150/150 attempted and reviewed in C++**.
At least **12 core data structures/algorithms implemented from scratch**.
At least **50 important problems re-solved** without looking at the prior solution.
At least **15 timed interview-style sessions/mocks** by the end of the buffer month.
A concise personal pattern cheat sheet and mistake log.
cppSkills: Inheritance and virtual functions at conceptual level
Time/space implications of common STL operations
readyItems: Recognize likely patterns without being told the topic.
Produce a reasonable brute-force solution quickly.
Improve it using the constraints and data-structure properties.
Write C++ without fighting basic syntax.
Reason correctly about time and space complexity.
Handle edge cases and test your code methodically.
Solve most familiar-pattern mediums in ~20–35 minutes.
Make structured progress on unfamiliar/hard problems rather than freezing.
Reconstruct important solutions weeks later instead of memorizing code.

milestones.text: Comfortable with core C++ syntax, references and pointers; LeetCode has begun.
Comfortable with vector/string, classes, linked lists, stacks/queues, hashing, recursion and core STL.
Comfortable with trees, BSTs, heaps and graph fundamentals.
Major graph and binary-search concepts understood; pattern recognition noticeably stronger.
Backtracking and dynamic programming are no longer mysterious; can derive states/transitions.
Primary curriculum complete; Top Interview 150 target complete; transition to interview hardening.
Buffer complete; weak areas repaired; repeated timed practice completed.

bufferWeeks.title: Buffer Week 1
tasks: Finish any missed LearnCpp / Grokking sections.
Finish any incomplete Top Interview 150 problems.

bufferWeeks.title: Buffer Week 2
tasks: Repair the two weakest DSA topics.
Re-implement 3 weak data structures without notes.

bufferWeeks.title: Buffer Week 3
tasks: Solve mixed unseen problems without sorting by topic first.
Force pattern identification before opening hints.
Review STL, ownership, references/pointers, comparators, and common syntax.

bufferWeeks.title: Buffer Week 4
tasks: Review complexity, edge cases, and testing habits.

bufferWeeks.title: Final contingency
tasks: Complete one final mock plus light review.
